proof_proposal.argument: At p0=gamma0(u1), set T_lambda=partial0/sqrt(-g_lambda(partial0,partial0)); it is well-defined and future timelike for small lambda. Initial metric Gram matrices remain positive definite near lambda0. Solve the coordinate geodesic ODE with this initial point/velocity. Christoffels are smooth jointly and Gamma_0=0, so on a fixed compact state neighborhood of the background line |Gamma_lambda|<=C|lambda|. While velocity remains in a fixed bounded neighborhood, |v_lambda-v0|<=|v_lambda(u1)-v0|+Cprime|lambda|T and |gamma_lambda-gamma0|<=T sup|v_lambda-v0|. Choose lambda small relative to the positive margins of that state neighborhood. The trajectory cannot leave it. At any putative finite maximal endpoint, bounded ODE derivative makes its state Cauchy, its limit remains in the interior, and local existence/uniqueness extends it, contradiction. Thus solutions exist on the entire fixed interval. The smooth parameter-dependence theorem, applied on a finite subdivision, gives smooth dependence on lambda through it. This derives common-interval existence rather than adding an unexplained family assumption.

Parallel transport the spatial frame along gamma_lambda by the linear coordinate equation Eprime=-Gamma_lambda(v_lambda,E).
